report.summary: The team has substantively closed the prior memory-safety backlog in this scope: H5 (destroy fallback), H6 (memory bounds overflow), H9 (unaligned reinterpret_cast), M7, M8 (sentinel handle), M9 (config string deep-copy), M11, and C2 are all genuinely resolved, with real fixes rather than cosmetic ones. However, the recently expanded V5 load path (RAM/VRAM RLE sub-blocks) introduced a NEW critical heap buffer overflow reachable from the public legends_load_state(): the engine deserializer overwrites ctx->memory.size from an attacker-controlled uint64_t and then uses it as the RLE decompression capacity with no check against the real allocation, so a tiny crafted blob (plain-CRC32 protected) writes far past a ~704KB buffer. There is also a create error-path engine-handle leak that permanently bricks the library, and M6 remains partially open because event callbacks are still invoked unguarded across the C ABI. Integrity is plain CRC32 (not a MAC) at both layers, so crafted save states are trivially constructed. Overall: good remediation discipline, but a corruption bug and a library-bricking leak sit in the freshly grown code.

findings.title: Heap buffer overflow: dosbox_lib_load_state trusts attacker-controlled memory.size as RLE decode capacity
findings.evidence: dosbox_library.cpp:1303 does `ctx->memory.size = static_cast<size_t>(mem.size)` from a uint64_t save field (engine_state.h:265) with no validation. memory.base is a fixed `bytes+65536` allocation made once (dosbox_context.cpp:39-41) and there is no separate capacity field. The RAM sub-block then calls zero_rle_decode(..., ctx->memory.base, ctx->memory.size) (1444) using the corrupted size as cap; zero_rle_decode honors cap (zero_rle.h:84-117) but cap is now attacker-chosen, and RLE expands a few input bytes into memory.size zero bytes. Reachable via public legends_load_state, which forwards the engine slice after only checking offsets are inside the legends buffer (legends_embed_api.cpp:2442-2449). Integrity is plain CRC32 (dosbox_library.cpp:1129-1136), trivially forged. Same corrupted size also drives the reset guard memset (522-527) and all read/write bounds checks (1723,1747).
findings.recommendation: Never overwrite ctx->memory.size from the save; validate mem.size == create-time allocation and reject on mismatch. Clamp RAM/VRAM decode cap to the true allocated size independently of any deserialized field. Add an engine-memory-field fuzz target.

findings.title: Engine handle leak on legends_create error path bricks the library (g_instance_exists stuck true)
findings.evidence: legends_create's terminal catch (legends_embed_api.cpp:951-957) does inst->machine.reset(); g_active_instance.store(nullptr); delete inst; but never calls dosbox_lib_destroy(inst->engine_handle). dosbox_lib_create/init may already have succeeded (905-923), setting the engine g_instance_exists=true and allocating g_context. A throw after init — e.g. load_embedded_font()'s vector assign can throw bad_alloc (939; instance_state.h:161-164) — leaks the engine and leaves g_instance_exists=true, so every later dosbox_lib_create returns DOSBOX_LIB_ERR_ALREADY_CREATED (dosbox_library.cpp:360-363) until process restart. The init-failure branch (914-922) handles cleanup correctly; the catch does not. Catch also lacks catch(...), so a non-std throw escapes the extern "C" boundary (UB).
findings.recommendation: In the catch, destroy inst->engine_handle if non-null before delete inst; add a catch(...) arm that does the same.

findings.title: Event callbacks invoked unguarded across the C ABI (M6 still partially open)
findings.evidence: fire_event() calls cb.fn(...) with no try/catch (legends_embed_api.cpp:744-749). It is invoked from extern "C" functions with no surrounding try/catch: legends_mount_drive (2809,2814) and legends_unmount_drive (2841,2846). A throwing C++ embedder callback unwinds across the C ABI -> UB. The log-callback half of M6 is fixed (instance_state.h:50-57) but the event-callback half is not; fire_event in legends_step_cycles is only safe by accident of that function's own try/catch (1084,1177).
findings.recommendation: Wrap the cb.fn(...) call inside fire_event in try{...}catch(...){} mirroring LogState::log.

findings.title: Cross-layer load atomicity gap: engine committed before wrapper staging can fail
findings.evidence: legends_load_state mutates engine state in Phase 2 (2435-2453) before staging wrapper sections. Phase 3 staged_indexed_pixels.resize() can throw bad_alloc, which is caught and returns LEGENDS_ERR_OUT_OF_MEMORY (2504-2509) without reverting the engine, leaving the engine on the new state while wrapper time/frame/pic/input state stay old -> silent desync producing wrong hashes/frames. Same shape in the V2 loader (2228-2237).
findings.recommendation: Stage all allocations (including indexed_pixels) before the engine load, or snapshot/rollback engine state if wrapper staging fails.

findings.title: Non-portable raw-struct serialization with indeterminate padding in V3 saves
findings.evidence: ScheduledEvent (instance_state.h:303-310: uint32_t id then uint64_t deadline -> 4-byte padding, sizeof 24) and the SaveStateTime/CPU/PIC/Frame headers are written by raw memcpy of structs with native byte order and indeterminate padding (legends_embed_api.cpp:1889,1900,1908,1927-1930,1967), despite the format being labeled portable. Padding bytes are CRC-covered, so logically identical states need not byte-match and cross-ABI loads mis-deserialize. Does not affect legends_get_state_hash (field-level) or single-platform round-trips, hence low.
findings.recommendation: Field-serialize these sections with the existing little-endian helpers (as already done for InputEvent/DMAChannelState), or zero-init structs and document the format as platform-local.

sprint_recommendations: Harden untrusted deserialization: validate every length/size/offset in both save formats against real allocations, clamp all decode caps independently of deserialized fields (fixes mem-01), field-serialize padded structs (mem-05), and add an engine-memory/RAM-blob-targeted fuzz target.

Error-path resource safety at the C ABI: audit every extern "C" entry point for engine-handle cleanup on all throw/early-return paths (mem-02) and exception containment around every embedder callback via fire_event (mem-03); add catch(...) arms.
Load atomicity: move all wrapper-layer allocations ahead of any engine mutation, or add engine snapshot/rollback, so a failed load leaves the machine unchanged (mem-04).
Consider upgrading save-state integrity from plain CRC32 toward a keyed/authenticated check, since CRC offers no protection against crafted states that drive mem-01-class bugs.

verdict.note:
VERIFIED REAL after attempting refutation on every cited line; all hold up.

(1) Cited lines say what is claimed:
- dosbox_library.cpp:1303 — `ctx->memory.size = static_cast<size_t>(mem.size)` copies the save's uint64 size field with no validation. CONFIRMED.
- engine_state.h:265 — `uint64_t size` is the first field of attacker-deserialized EngineStateMemory. CONFIRMED.
- dosbox_context.cpp:39-41 — base = `new uint8_t[bytes + 65536]()`, `memory.size = bytes`. memory.size IS the only capacity field; base is a fixed one-time allocation. CONFIRMED. (Production allocator memory.cpp:315/356 behaves the same.)
- zero_rle.h:84-117 — decode honors `cap` (out>=cap / out+count>cap return 0) but writes up to cap; literal non-zero bytes are copied verbatim from src (line 94), so attacker controls length AND content. CONFIRMED.
- dosbox_library.cpp:1437-1444 — RAM subtag calls zero_rle_decode(..., ctx->memory.base, ctx->memory.size) using the size set at 1303. CONFIRMED.
- legends_embed_api.cpp:2440-2446 — public load path only VALIDATE_DATA_BOUNDS(engine_offset, engine_size) inside the legends buffer, then forwards the slice to dosbox_lib_load_state. CONFIRMED reachable from untrusted save.
- Integrity is plain unkeyed CRC32 (1129-1136), recomputed over the data — trivially forged after tampering. CONFIRMED.
- Reset memset (522-527) and read/write bounds (1723,1747) all use the same corrupted memory.size. CONFIRMED secondary corruption surface.

(2) Refutation attempts all fail:
- Guard at 1440 `if (entry.orig_size > ctx->memory.size) break` compares attacker-controlled orig_size against the ALREADY-corrupted memory.size, so it does not constrain anything; and orig_size is never passed to the decoder, so the only write bound is cap=memory.size.
- Grepped memory.size/mem.size across the file and memory.base assignments across engine/src: between line 1303 and the RAM decode there is NO re-validation or clamp, and memory.base is never reallocated during load (only assigned in the create-time allocators). So base stays sized to configured RAM while size is overwritten to an attacker value (e.g., GB-scale), defeating the 64KB HLT guard.
- Offset validation at 1138-1156 checks only that memory_offset is a valid location to read the struct, never that mem.size equals the real allocation.

(3) Severity critical is justified: a controlled-length, partially controlled-content heap write primitive reachable by loading a forged save state, protected only by a forgeable CRC32, with the same poisoned size also corrupting reset and all subsequent memory read/write bounds. The recommendation (never overwrite memory.size from the save; clamp decode cap to the true allocation; reject on size mismatch; add a fuzz target) is correct.

Verified all cited evidence by direct read. legends_embed_api.cpp:951-957 catch(const std::exception&) does machine.reset()/g_active_instance=null/delete inst but never dosbox_lib_destroy(inst->engine_handle); contrast with the correct init-failure branch at 914-923 which does call it (916). struct legends_instance (src/legends/internal/legends_instance.h) has no destructor and destroy_cleanup() explicitly does not free the engine handle, so delete inst leaks it. dosbox_library.cpp: g_instance_exists set true at 360 and reset only on create's own failures (371/376/430) or dosbox_lib_destroy (493); after successful dosbox_lib_init the only reset is dosbox_lib_destroy. Since the catch never sets *handle_out and deletes inst, legends_destroy (the only other dosbox_lib_destroy caller, line 984) is unreachable — every later create fails with ALREADY_CREATED until process restart, exactly as claimed. Missing catch(...) in extern "C" legends_create also confirmed (block spans 753-3220). One tempering fact: I checked every statement after successful init (lines 924-949); time_state/frame_state/input_state resets and init_test_pattern use fixed std::arrays (non-throwing), so the only realistic throw site is load_embedded_font's ~4KB vector assign (instance_state.h:161-164) throwing bad_alloc — an OOM-only trigger, making likelihood low. Impact (unrecoverable process-wide brick of an embeddable C API) and the trivial fix justify keeping it real; high severity is defensible though medium-high would also be reasonable given the OOM-only trigger.

report.summary: Save-state deserialization is genuinely well-hardened in both the legends layer (legends_embed_api.cpp) and engine bridge (dosbox_library.cpp): magic/version/size-underflow/CRC32 checks, overflow-safe subtraction-form bounds macros, count caps, pre-validation of input-event types, and four-phase atomic load. Prior findings H6 (memory-bounds overflow) and H9 (unaligned reinterpret_cast) are fixed; H7 (HashMode::Full) is partially fixed (RAM now hashed, VGA/device still not). The weak surface is the newer IPC/shared-memory isolation layer — the MIT-shell to GPL-engine-host trust boundary that by design runs untrusted guest code. Framebuffer/audio SHM consumers trust attacker-mappable geometry fields and read out of bounds in the trusted shell; the proxy never validates response type or sequence id; endpoints have no peer authentication and use predictable, world-reachable names; and the 89-struct/43-case IPC parser is entirely unfuzzed. The GPL isolation guarantees (REQ-ISO-016 symbol scan, crash recovery, SHM write path) are unverified — IPC mode is functional transport but not yet a real security boundary. IPC is opt-in (off by default), which bounds present exposure, but it is the roadmap direction.

findings.title: Shared-memory consumers trust attacker-controlled geometry → OOB read in trusted shell
findings.evidence: FramebufferShm::read_if_new computes pixel_bytes = current_width*current_height*4 from SHM-resident header fields (written by the untrusted engine host) with no clamp to max_width/max_height or buf_size_, and returns a span of that length. legends_capture_rgb sets *size_out to that value and memcpy's frame->pixels.size() out of a buffer sized only for max_w*max_h*4 — a host setting current_width=current_height=0xFFFF causes a multi-GB OOB read. map_pointers derives buf_size_ from SHM-resident max_width/max_height rather than the mapped size. AudioRingBuffer::map_pointers caches capacity_/channels_ from the SHM header; pop/push index samples_[(idx%capacity_)*channels_] and divide by channels_, so an inflated capacity or channels==0 yields OOB access or divide-by-zero.
findings.recommendation: Validate all consumer-side geometry against the actually-mapped region size: clamp current_*<=max_*, require pixel_bytes<=buf_size_, reject channels==0 and capacity_frames larger than mapped; never recompute buffer extents from SHM-resident fields.

findings.title: Proxy does not validate response message type or sequence id
findings.evidence: ProxyConnection::request<Resp> deserializes whatever bytes arrive as the expected Resp type; send_and_recv returns the first message read after sending with no check that header.msg_type==Resp::type or header.sequence_id==seq. The protocol defines an unsolicited push EventNotification=0x1102; if emitted it is consumed as the next request's response and desynchronizes the stream. A wrongly-typed but large-enough payload deserializes successfully and is read as a valid error_code/result (e.g. a forged LEGENDS_OK).
findings.recommendation: In send_and_recv, loop until a response whose msg_type and sequence_id match the request; route EventNotification to a separate queue.

findings.title: IPC endpoints lack peer authentication and use predictable, world-reachable names
findings.evidence: No check that the peer is the spawned engine host; handshake carries no token. POSIX server socket at /tmp/legends_<pid>.sock (predictable, world-writable /tmp), created with process umask, no SO_PEERCRED on accept; shm_open uses O_CREAT|O_RDWR|0600 with no O_EXCL. Windows CreateNamedPipeA passes nullptr security attrs with no FILE_FLAG_FIRST_PIPE_INSTANCE (name squatting) and no PIPE_REJECT_REMOTE_CLIENTS; CreateFileMappingA uses default DACL with no ERROR_ALREADY_EXISTS check.
findings.recommendation: Add peer-credential checks (SO_PEERCRED/getpeereid, GetNamedPipeClientProcessId), set FILE_FLAG_FIRST_PIPE_INSTANCE + PIPE_REJECT_REMOTE_CLIENTS + owner-only DACL, use O_EXCL on SHM create, use unguessable per-launch names in a 0700 dir, and add a handshake nonce.

findings.title: IPC parsing layer (108 message types, 89 structs, 43-case dispatcher) is entirely unfuzzed
findings.evidence: The only fuzz targets are fuzz_legends_load_state, fuzz_engine_load_state, fuzz_input_injection, fuzz_config_parser. The IPC surface — MessageCodec/MessageHeader framing, ~89 hand-written deserialize() functions, and the 43-case dispatch() — parses untrusted bytes at the GPL trust boundary but has no fuzz target. Existing unit tests (test_ipc_messages.cpp etc.) use well-formed inputs only.
findings.recommendation: Add a libFuzzer target feeding raw bytes through MessageCodec::feed/try_decode and dispatch(), plus one driving each proxy-side Resp::deserialize; wire into the existing CI fuzz job.

findings.title: GPL process-isolation guarantees unverified; missing half is assurance, not plumbing
findings.evidence: LEGENDS_USE_IPC builds legends_engine_host + legends_proxy and a CI job configures/builds/unit-tests IPC mode, but: there is no REQ-ISO-016 GPL symbol-isolation scan (CI only does test -f build/legends_engine_host), so the core GPL-compliance guarantee that no aibox_core/legends_core symbols leak into the proprietary shell is unenforced; no REQ-ISO-013 crash detection/recovery (heartbeat/crash_handler exist but host loop has no watchdog); and engine_host main.cpp connects only the control channel and never opens the framebuffer/audio SHM, so the write path is unwired. TODO/roadmap mark REQ-ISO-003..016 Missing while the mechanism is substantially built, understating the code and overstating the guarantees.
findings.recommendation: Implement the REQ-ISO-016 symbol-scan as a CI gate, wire crash detection/recovery, finish the SHM write path, and reconcile TODO/roadmap status with the shipped code.

findings.title: MountDriveReq path length truncated to 8 bits while full bytes are copied
findings.evidence: MountDriveReq::serialize writes the path length as write_u8(buf,5,static_cast<uint8_t>(host_path.size())) but serialized_size_dynamic() and the memcpy use the full host_path.size(); a path >255 bytes records a wrapped length and deserialize reconstructs a silently truncated path. Mount host paths feed path-confinement (REQ-SEC-023 canonical resolution), so truncation can resolve to an unintended directory.
findings.recommendation: Use a u16/u32 length field and reject oversize paths explicitly.

findings.title: Memory-bounds integer overflow now uses overflow-safe subtraction form
findings.evidence: dosbox_lib_read_memory and dosbox_lib_write_memory now check `size > g_context->memory.size || address > g_context->memory.size - size`, which cannot wrap, instead of the prior address+size form. Confirmed fixed at HEAD.
findings.recommendation: No action needed; close prior H6. Keep the subtraction-form pattern in any new bounds checks.

findings.title: HashMode::Full still omits VGA registers/VRAM and device state
findings.evidence: HashMode::Full now hashes all conventional RAM (builder.update(ctx->memory.base, ctx->memory.size)) — an improvement over the prior 'FULL_MODE' marker — but the in-code comment confirms VGA registers/VRAM and device state are still not hashed ('VGA and device state will be added in Phase B serialization'). The header's documented contract is closer but not yet met.
findings.recommendation: Extend HashMode::Full to hash VGA registers/VRAM and device state, or narrow the documented contract until then.

sprint_recommendations: Harden the shared-memory boundary: clamp/validate all consumer-side framebuffer and audio geometry against the mapped region size, and add response-type + sequence-id matching plus an event queue in the proxy (SEC-01, SEC-02) — these are the directly exploitable items reachable from a compromised engine host.

Authenticate and lock down IPC endpoints: peer-credential checks, FILE_FLAG_FIRST_PIPE_INSTANCE / PIPE_REJECT_REMOTE_CLIENTS / owner-only DACLs, O_EXCL on SHM, unguessable per-launch names, and a handshake nonce (SEC-03).
Fuzz the IPC surface: byte-level libFuzzer targets for MessageCodec + dispatch() and for each proxy-side Resp::deserialize, wired into the existing CI fuzz job (SEC-04).

Make GPL isolation a verifiable guarantee: add the REQ-ISO-016 symbol-isolation CI gate, crash detection/recovery, finish the SHM write path, and reconcile TODO/roadmap status with the shipped code (SEC-05).

verdict.note: Verified all cited lines; code descriptions are accurate but the claimed high-severity trusted-shell OOB does not hold up. (1) Framebuffer: the memcpy at src/legends_proxy/proxy_api.cpp:230 is guarded by `if (buffer && buffer_size >= frame->pixels.size())`. The finding's exact scenario (host sets current_width=current_height=0xFFFF -> pixel_bytes~17GB, caller buffer "sized only for max_w*max_h*4"~8MB) makes the guard FALSE, so the memcpy is SKIPPED -> no OOB. An OOB would require the caller to pass a destination buffer LARGER than max_w*max_h*4, the opposite of the cited trigger; the finding omits this guard. (2) Audio: trust direction is inverted. proxy_connection.cpp:24-29 shows the trusted proxy/shell CREATES both SHM regions ("server side creates them") with channels=2, capacity=audio_ring_frames(2048); create() rejects channels==0/capacity==0 (audio_ring.cpp:21). For audio, create sets header fields BEFORE map_pointers (audio_ring.cpp:32-41), so the consumer caches channels_=2,capacity_=2048 at creation, before the engine connects. pop() (only trusted-shell consumer, proxy_api.cpp:315) uses these CACHED members, NOT live header fields, so a malicious engine writing channels=0 or inflated capacity into SHM cannot reach the proxy: no divide-by-zero (divides by 2), and ri%capacity_ stays within the proxy-sized samples_ array (avail clamped to capacity_, to_read clamped to caller buffer). push() runs in the untrusted engine's own process, not the trusted shell. (3) buf_size_ derives from max_width/max_height which are proxy-written (trusted), not attacker-controlled. Production wiring: FramebufferShm::open/AudioRingBuffer::open/begin_write/end_write have no production callers (only benchmarks/tests); only read_if_new and pop are trusted-shell consumers. Residual minor gap: read_if_new lacks a current<=max clamp and *size_out can return an inflated value (proxy_api.cpp:227) -- worth hardening as defense-in-depth, but not the exploitable high OOB claimed. Files: src/legends_ipc/framebuffer_shm.cpp:74-92,9-15; src/legends_ipc/audio_ring.cpp:10-16,21,32-41,63-110; src/legends_proxy/proxy_api.cpp:222-232,309-317; src/legends_proxy/proxy_connection.cpp:24-29.

VERIFIED — every cited line and every sub-claim checks out; severity high is justified. (1) Citations accurate: ci.yml:93-127 linux-ipc job builds with -DLEGENDS_USE_IPC=ON and its only isolation "verification" is `test -f build/legends_engine_host` plus generic ctest — no symbol scan step. CMakeLists.txt:372-434 defines legends_engine_host (links GPL legends_core) and legends_proxy (MIT, links only legends_ipc). roadmap.md:3319-3332 marks REQ-ISO-003..016 all "Missing"; TODO.md:19 says GPL isolation is "STUB, 2 of 16" — yet the serialization lib, control channel, SHM framebuffer, audio ring, host exe, proxy lib, compile switch, and CI job all exist, so docs understate the code exactly as claimed. (2) Attempted refutations failed. (a) Symbol scan: a scanner DOES exist (scripts/verify_gpl_isolation.py, cmake/VerifyGPLIsolation.cmake, tests/scripts/test_verify_gpl_isolation.py) — but VerifyGPLIsolation.cmake is never include()d in any CMakeLists (grep of all *.cmake/CMakeLists.txt: only self-reference in its own usage comment), the script is invoked by no CI workflow, and its self-test is not registered in CTest. Worse, CMakeLists.txt:362 asserts "verified by REQ-ISO-003 and REQ-ISO-016" — an assertion that never executes. So the enforcement gap is real and slightly worse than stated (assurance exists as dead code). (b) Crash detection: HeartbeatMonitor (src/legends_proxy/heartbeat.cpp) and CrashHandler (crash_handler.cpp, with restart()) are implemented and unit-tested (tests/unit/test_heartbeat.cpp, test_crash_handler.cpp), but grep shows zero instantiation in proxy_api.cpp/proxy_connection.cpp — not wired into the production connection lifecycle; also HeartbeatMonitor::heartbeat_loop returns permanently after one timeout. (c) SHM write path: proxy_connection.cpp:25-28 CREATEs FramebufferShm/AudioRingBuffer, but engine_host main.cpp only #includes the headers (lines 9-10) and never calls FramebufferShm::open/AudioRingBuffer::open; engine_dispatcher.cpp (~45 message handlers, the only other host logic) never touches SHM, and no CaptureFramebuffer message exists — so video/audio cannot flow in IPC mode. Host CLI requires --shm but the value is parsed and never used to map memory. (3) Severity: high is fair — the GPL-compliance guarantee is the legal core of the IPC architecture, the codebase claims verification that never runs, and CI's existence-check gives false assurance. Only softening factor: IPC mode is an opt-in build (not necessarily the shipped default), and the structural mechanism (proxy links only MIT legends_ipc) is sound plumbing; the finding itself already frames this correctly as "missing half is assurance, not plumbing."

findings.title: C2 'fix' is vacuous: library build links no-op PIC_RunQueue stub; no timer ticks or IRQ delivery during any legends step
findings.evidence: cpu_bridge.cpp:113 calls PIC_RunQueue() labeled '(C2 fix)', but AIBOX_CORE_SOURCES compiles cpu_library_stubs.cpp whose PIC_RunQueue is 'Stub: no PIC event queue in library mode yet' returning false; hardware/pic.cpp appears in no CMake target; legends_core links aibox_core. TIMER_AddTick is never called on the step path, so PIT/keyboard IRQs and per-ms handlers never fire and events_processed is always 0. CPU_Check_NMI does resolve to the real cpu.cpp:635 implementation. Latent bug: real PIC_RunQueue does CPU_CycleLeft+=CPU_Cycles; CPU_Cycles=0, which would corrupt the bridge's consumed=budget-CPU_Cycles accounting (cpu_bridge.cpp:110-130) when integrated.
findings.recommendation: Integrate a deterministic PIC/PIT event queue into library mode (compile pic.cpp behind DOSBOX_LIBRARY_MODE guards or build a minimal Scheduler.tla-conformant queue); restructure execute_cycles into per-ms slices (PIC_RunQueue -> decoder -> TIMER_AddTick) with corrected cycle accounting; serialize the queue in save states; make events_processed truthful.

findings.title: Two unsynchronized thread_local context globals remain (aibox + dosbox layers)
findings.evidence: Both thread_local g_current_context pointers still exist. Mitigated since Feb: legends_step_cycles now installs both dosbox::ContextGuard and legends::compat::ContextGuard for the full step scope including input draining; engine entry points install their own guards. Residual risk is non-step engine paths consulting aibox::compat::current() without the legends guard.
findings.recommendation: Either merge to a single TLS context pointer or add a debug assertion that both pointers reference the same logical instance whenever either compat::current() is consulted. Downgrade from high to medium given guard coverage.

findings.title: Dead stub execution path still present: MachineContext::step()/run(), dosbox_step(), 7 init_* no-ops
findings.evidence: MachineContext::step() is still a counter-incrementing no-op, now with a DEPRECATED(M10) banner; run() busy-loops on it. dosbox_step() carries the same banner and its only callers are engine/tests/unit/test_dosbox_context.cpp:382,404. The 7 init stubs (H4) return Ok() immediately, documented as 'intentional no-ops' delegating to the engine bridge. Covers prior H3, H4, and M10 jointly: quarantined and documented but not removed; the stub still silently reports success.
findings.recommendation: Delete MachineContext::step()/run(), dosbox_step(), the 7 init stubs and their forward-declared phantom classes; port the two unit tests to dosbox_lib_step_cycles. Closes H3/H4/M10 permanently.

findings.title: Reentrancy guard extended to core APIs but missing on mount/unmount, joystick, and Phase-3 setters
findings.evidence: in_step is now checked in reset, step_cycles, key_event, key_event_ext, text_input, mouse_event, save_state, load_state (lines 1010, 1076, 1509, 1527, 1544, 1599, 1854, 2287) with a scope guard clearing on all exits. Mutating APIs added since lack it: legends_mount_drive (2755), legends_unmount_drive (2819), legends_joystick_event (2906), midi/printer/ipx/glide/pc98 setters (2959-3155). TLA ReentrancyMinimal PhaseConsistent/CallbackSafe remain PARTIAL.
findings.recommendation: Add the one-line in_step check to every remaining state-mutating API; add a callback-reentrancy unit test that exercises mount and joystick from a log callback.

findings.title: MixerState/audio thread safety substantially fixed in library mode, but conformance is partly vacuous (no audio is ever produced)
findings.evidence: MixerState ring indices are now std::atomic; BufferAudio is mutex-protected; the PAL SDL2 sink uses a correct acquire/release SPSC ring. Residual races: BufferAudio::push_samples reads is_open_/paused_ before locking and pause() writes paused_ unlocked; the SDL2 audio callback reads non-atomic volume_. Critically, aibox::headless::PushAudioSamples has zero production callers (tests only) and nothing pushes into buffer_audio(), so dosbox_lib_get_audio_samples always returns 0 samples — the ThreadSafety invariant is satisfied largely because no audio callback thread exists in library mode.
findings.recommendation: Fix the two residual benign races (atomic flags/volume); when mixer output is wired into library mode, drive per-ms mixing from virtual step time, not the SDL callback clock, to preserve determinism.

findings.title: dosbox_lib_get_context_ptr now enforces LIB_CHECK_THREAD
findings.evidence: Function now begins with LIB_VALIDATE_HANDLE, LIB_CHECK_THREAD() (line 660), null-pointer and init checks. Closes the ThreadingMinimal CoreSingleThreaded/WrongThreadBlocked partial conformance from TLA_CONFORMANCE.md section 3.
findings.recommendation: Mark resolved in AUDIT.md and TLA_CONFORMANCE.md; no further action.

findings.title: Determinism verification hash (Fast mode) excludes CPU GPRs/EIP/EFLAGS and all RAM/VRAM contents
findings.evidence: dosbox_lib_get_state_hash uses HashMode::Fast. CpuState::hash_into hashes only cycle counters and NMI/halted flags — no GPRs/EIP/segments (those live in global cpu_regs, only captured by snapshot_cpu_gprs during save_state). MemoryState::hash_into hashes metadata only ('We do NOT hash the actual memory contents in Fast mode'); RAM is Full-mode only and nothing calls Full. legends_verify_determinism and all hash-comparing determinism tests (test_determinism_at_scale.cpp:78-127, determinism_harness.h:93-97) therefore cannot detect divergence in registers or memory — the most likely real divergence. TLA_CONFORMANCE marks TraceDeterminism CONFORMANT, which is overstated.
findings.recommendation: Add GPR/EIP/EFLAGS/segment state to the Fast hash (snapshot_cpu_gprs helper already exists); run determinism CI tests with a Full-mode hash including RAM/VRAM; correct the TraceDeterminism rating until done.

findings.title: legends_joystick_event mutates guest RAM then returns LEGENDS_ERR_NOT_SUPPORTED; bypasses in_step guard and deterministic input queue
findings.evidence: Function writes joystick axis/button state directly into guest BDA memory via dosbox_lib_write_memory (lines 2938, 2953) and then 'return LEGENDS_ERR_NOT_SUPPORTED;' (line 2955) — error returned after successful mutation, violating the error model (REQ-EX-004 / ErrorModel SuccessRequiresValidState). It also lacks the in_step reentrancy check that key/mouse have, and bypasses the sequenced input queue drained at step start, so joystick input is unordered relative to key/mouse for replay and invisible to the determinism hash. Appears to be a collision between commit 7f86dd7 (stubs return NOT_SUPPORTED) and 4b4c43b (real joystick bridge).
findings.recommendation: Return LEGENDS_OK on success, add the in_step guard, and route joystick through the input queue as a third InputEventType so replay ordering and hashing cover it.

findings.title: IPC proxy never matches responses by sequence_id or msg_type; one recv timeout permanently desynchronizes the protocol
findings.evidence: ProxyConnection::request<Resp> deserializes whatever message arrives next; send_and_recv sends with a fresh sequence_id (line 80) then recv(5000) hardcoded (line 85) without comparing header.msg_type or sequence_id, even though the engine host echoes sequence_id (main.cpp:94-96). A step_ms or save_state exceeding 5s times out, leaves the late response in the pipe, and every subsequent RPC reads the wrong (off-by-one) response, silently misdeserialized. The dormant HeartbeatMonitor sends on the same channel from its own thread without the connection mutex — a second desync source if ever wired.
findings.recommendation: Loop recv discarding mismatched sequence_ids, verify response msg_type against Resp::type, treat timeout as channel-desync requiring drain/reconnect, make timeouts per-operation, and route heartbeats through the connection mutex.

findings.title: Cross-process audio ring violates SPSC: writer mutates read_index on overflow, racing the reader's read-modify-write
findings.evidence: push() advances and stores read_index when full (lines 73-74) while pop() does an unconditional store of its stale local ri (line 108) — lost updates cause re-read of overwritten frames, duplicated/torn audio, and miscomputed availability. Indices are modded by capacity so memory safety holds. Additionally open()/map_pointers trusts capacity_frames/channels from the shared header; a zero value makes 'wi % capacity_' divide by zero in the embedder process.
findings.recommendation: Writer must never touch read_index: drop incoming frames when full (or CAS read_index for drop-oldest); validate header capacity/channels against expected values on open().

findings.title: TSan is allow_failure in CI with known, named data races (g_active_instance, CrashBreadcrumb::add)
findings.evidence: CI comment: 'TSan detects pre-existing data races in engine global state (g_active_instance), CrashBreadcrumb::add(), and cross-thread tests... Mark allow-failure until REQ-TH-004 mixer/global state fixes land.' The mixer fixes (M3) substantially landed but allow_failure:true remains, so new concurrency regressions merge silently and the named races are untriaged in any audit doc.
findings.recommendation: Triage remaining TSan reports, suppress only the intentional wrong-thread tests, fix the named races, remove allow_failure so the sanitizer gates merges.

findings.title: TLA_CONFORMANCE.md stale: 4 of 5 non-conformant invariants fixed at HEAD but undocumented; legends event queue is vestigial; memory_kb still unvalidated
findings.evidence: At HEAD: HandleConsistency and NullHandleConsistent fixed (get_instance strict handle match); BufferNotCorrupted fixed (transactional text_input slot pre-check); cpu_cycles range-validated (841-847) though memory_kb still flows unchecked into memory_size (line 871) and audio_rate is absent; MixerState largely fixed. The doc (dated 2026-02-24) reports all five as NON-CONFORMANT. Conversely EventCount/EventDigestPreserved are vacuous: EventQueueState has no producer anywhere — only serialized (1921-1928), restored (2205, 2480), and hashed (2618-2623), always empty.
findings.recommendation: Re-baseline TLA_CONFORMANCE.md against HEAD with file:line anchors; validate memory_kb range in legends_create; either wire the event queue to real scheduled events (with conc-01) or delete it.

findings.title: IPC runtime parity gap: shared-memory framebuffer/audio regions have no producer in engine_host; IPC capture_rgb silently returns empty
findings.evidence: The proxy's legends_capture_rgb reads the SHM framebuffer via fb->read_if_new(0) and returns LEGENDS_OK with 0 bytes when empty; ProxyConnection::connect creates both SHM regions. On the host side FramebufferShm/AudioRingBuffer are only #included in main.cpp — the 43-case dispatcher never opens or writes either region, and step handlers do not publish frames. InProcess vs Ipc runtimes therefore diverge observably (silent success with no data) — the successor to M10's dual-path divergence, one layer up. TODO.md GPL Process Isolation is 2/16, so likely known-incomplete, but the silent-success failure mode is unrecorded.
findings.recommendation: Publish framebuffer (and audio) into SHM after each step in the engine host loop with a sequence bump; until then, return LEGENDS_ERR_NOT_SUPPORTED from IPC capture_rgb rather than empty success; add a proxy-parity integration test comparing both runtimes.

report.summary: Thread discipline has genuinely improved since the 2026-02-24 audit: M7 is resolved, the handle-fallback (H5-class) and text_input non-conformances are fixed, the in_step guard now covers the core mutating APIs, and 4 of 5 NON-CONFORMANT TLA+ invariants are closed at HEAD — though TLA_CONFORMANCE.md was never re-baselined. The determinism story is weaker than documented: the headline C2 'fix' is vacuous because the library build links a no-op PIC_RunQueue stub (the real PIC is in no CMake target), so no timer ticks or IRQs ever fire during legends steps; the SHA-256 determinism oracle (Fast hash) excludes CPU GPRs/EIP and all RAM, blinding verify_determinism and the at-scale tests to the most likely divergence; and the legends event queue that the hash and save format cover is never populated. The newer IPC runtime adds protocol fragility (no response sequence/type matching, SPSC violation in the audio ring, SHM with no producer), and TSan remains allow-failure in CI with known races named in a comment. Single-owner-thread enforcement, input-queue ordering, and the fixed ms-to-cycles ratio are solid foundations; device-time integration and an honest oracle are the missing halves of the determinism promise.
sprint_recommendations: Make time real: integrate a deterministic PIC/PIT event queue into library mode, restructure execute_cycles into per-ms slices (PIC_RunQueue -> decoder -> TIMER_AddTick) with corrected CPU_Cycles/CPU_CycleLeft accounting, serialize the queue in save states, and make Scheduler/PIC TLA specs testable (closes C2 for real).

Trustworthy oracle: add GPRs/EIP/EFLAGS/segments to the Fast state hash and run determinism CI with Full-mode (RAM+VRAM) hashing; fix legends_joystick_event (error code, in_step guard, route through input queue); delete or wire the vestigial EventQueueState; re-baseline TLA_CONFORMANCE.md.

IPC protocol robustness: sequence/type matching and timeout-desync recovery in ProxyConnection, SPSC-correct audio ring, framebuffer/audio producers in engine_host after each step, heartbeat wired through the connection mutex.

Green TSan: fix the named g_active_instance and CrashBreadcrumb::add races plus residual BufferAudio/volume_ nits, suppress intentional wrong-thread tests, and remove allow_failure from the TSan CI job so concurrency regressions gate merges.

verdict.note: Verified all four citations directly; every claim holds. (1) dosbox_library.cpp:684: dosbox_lib_get_state_hash hard-codes dosbox::HashMode::Fast. (2) state_hash.cpp:300-305: RAM contents hashed only under `if (mode == HashMode::Full)`; in-code comment says VGA/device state "will be added in Phase B" even for Full. (3) dosbox_context.cpp:103-130: CpuState::hash_into hashes only cycle counters, auto-adjust flags, NMI flags, extflags_toggle, halted — no GPRs/EIP/EFLAGS/segments; those live in global cpu_regs/Segs and are read only by snapshot_cpu_gprs (cpu_bridge.cpp:166-179), invoked solely from the save_state path (dosbox_library.cpp:964), never from hashing. MemoryState::hash_into (dosbox_context.cpp:685-714) hashes layout metadata only, with explicit comment "We do NOT hash the actual memory contents in Fast mode". (4) legends_embed_api.cpp:2629-2696: legends_verify_determinism compares legends_get_state_hash outputs; that function (2552-2627) wraps the Fast engine hash plus input-queue/time/PIC/event-queue metadata — still no registers or RAM. Refutation attempts failed: grep shows HashMode::Full is called only by two unit tests checking hash-mode distinctness (test_dosbox_state_hash.cpp, test_dosbox_timing.cpp), never by any determinism verification path; determinism tests (tests/unit/test_determinism_at_scale.cpp:41-46, 78-127 via legends_get_state_hash; engine/tests/determinism/determinism_harness.h:93-97 via dosbox_lib_get_state_hash) all compare the Fast hash; the only full-buffer comparison test (test_portable_serialize.cpp DMAStateRoundTrip) is a save/load/save serialization check, not cross-run determinism, so it does not mitigate. TLA_CONFORMANCE.md:110 indeed marks TraceDeterminism CONFORMANT citing these tests. Severity high is justified for a project whose core claim is verified determinism: the verification hash is blind to architectural CPU state and all RAM/VRAM, so register- or memory-level divergence with matching cycle counts passes every determinism check (a false-negative verification gap, not runtime corruption). Minor nit only: "nothing calls Full" should read "no determinism path calls Full" — two hash-mode unit tests do call it.

Verified against source; could not refute. (1) Cited lines accurate: proxy_connection.h:41-44 request<Resp> blindly deserializes the next decoded message; proxy_connection.cpp:80-87 sends with fresh seq then recv(5000) hardcoded, never comparing header.sequence_id or msg_type (the proxy never reads seq from any response — grep confirms seq only appears on the send side); engine_host/main.cpp:94-96 and 85-87 echo sequence_id, so matching is possible but unused. (2) Desync mechanism confirmed one layer down: control_channel_win.cpp:156-181 recv feeds a persistent codec_ buffer and returns Timeout without discarding, so a late response is decoded by the next recv — permanent off-by-one thereafter. No mitigation exists: proxy_api.cpp maps timeout to an error code and continues on the same connection; no drain/resync/reconnect logic or tests anywhere (grep for desync/resync/drain). 'Silently misdeserialized' holds: messages.cpp deserializers check only minimum size, and many responses (incl. ErrorResponseMsg) share the identical 4-byte error_code layout. (3) Trigger plausible: engine_dispatcher.cpp:82-94 passes uncapped caller-controlled ms to legends_step_ms; SaveStateReq (503-523) serializes full state; VerifyDeterminism runs arbitrary test_cycles — any can exceed the fixed 5s budget. (4) Heartbeat claim accurate and fairly hedged: heartbeat.cpp:48-49 sends on the shared channel without the connection mutex, and HeartbeatMonitor is never instantiated (dormant). High severity justified: one slow RPC yields silent wrong results (step results, state hashes, save/load) on all subsequent calls in a project that documents determinism guarantees. Minor doc nit: control_channel.h:41 claims timeout returns BufferTooSmall but impl returns Timeout.

report.summary: The build/CI machinery has unusual breadth (4-sanitizer matrix, libFuzzer, 17 TLA+ checks, coverage with an 80% release gate, configure-time module-DAG verification, CPack for 3 platforms, centralized dependency pins), but enforcement collapsed one day before this audit: commit 6900e7a (2026-06-08) demoted sanitizers, fuzz, TLA+, static analysis, dependency scan, macOS, and SDL3 builds to nightly/manual-only, silently regressing prior-audit fixes H7/H8/M12 and contradicting ci.yml's own header and RELEASING.md. The flagship GPL-2.0 process-isolation promise has zero automated enforcement: VerifyGPLIsolation.cmake is never included anywhere and the DAG verifier hardcodes only 3 of 6 modules, skipping legends_ipc/legends_proxy/legends_engine_host. The release pipeline has never executed once (the repo has no git tags, so tag-gated packaging, NSIS/DMG, checksums, and the 80% coverage gate are all unexercised), and committed UTF-16 build logs show the maintainer's own Windows clang dev preset failing to compile and link on a toolchain no CI job covers. Prior findings L6 and L7 are resolved; L5 is narrowed but still open on Windows (hardcoded mingw32/SDL2 link against a nonexistent external/SDL2 tree).

findings.title: Quality gates demoted to nightly/manual: sanitizers, fuzz, TLA+, static analysis, dep-scan no longer run on PRs or merges (regresses H7/H8/M12); PR-fuzz step is unreachable dead code
findings.evidence: Commit 6900e7a (2026-06-08, 'Stabilize CI and RuntimeHost adoption') added `if: github.event_name == 'schedule' || github.event_name == 'workflow_dispatch'` to the sanitizers, fuzz, tlaplus, static-analysis, and dependency-scan jobs. The fuzz job's 'PR: Quick fuzz (30s)' step requires `github.event_name == 'pull_request'`, which the job-level if excludes, so it can never run. ci.yml:8-12 and RELEASING.md:7,38 still claim merge-to-main runs sanitizers and that sanitizers/fuzz/TLA+ must pass before tagging. ci.yml:11 promises nightly soak, but no workflow sets LEGENDS_SOAK_ENABLED and cmake/SoakTestLabels.cmake referenced at CMakeLists.txt:1020-1024 does not exist. TSan/MSan remain allow_failure (ci.yml:351-365) since March with no exit plan.
findings.recommendation: Restore sanitizers + fuzz + TLA+ on push to master/main per the documented tiering; fix the job-level if so the 30s PR fuzz step is reachable; set a dated exit plan for TSan/MSan allow-failure; implement or delete the soak claim; update RELEASING.md to match reality.

findings.title: GPL isolation is unenforced: VerifyGPLIsolation.cmake never included by any CMakeLists, and ModuleDAG verification skips legends_ipc/legends_proxy/legends_engine_host
findings.evidence: Grep for VerifyGPLIsolation across the repo finds no include() call — only the module itself, docs, and openspec. tasks.md:54 shows '[ ] 8.3 Linker verification: verify_gpl_isolation.py + CMake integration' unchecked. legends_verify_all_dags() (ModuleDAG.cmake:191-213) verifies only legends_core/legends_pal/aibox_core and legends_detect_cycles() hardcodes those 3 modules, while ModuleManifest.cmake:66-68 defines DAG entries for ipc/proxy/engine_host that nothing checks. The 'MUST NOT link GPL' constraints exist only as comments (CMakeLists.txt:361-362, 422-423). The only IPC CI job (linux-ipc) builds without PAL_BACKEND_SDL2/3, so project_legends (the target VerifyGPLIsolation instruments) would not exist even if included.
findings.recommendation: Extend legends_verify_all_dags to iterate every LEGENDS_DAG_* manifest entry; include VerifyGPLIsolation.cmake guarded on target existence; add an nm/verify_gpl_isolation.py CI step over liblegends_proxy.a and liblegends_ipc.a in linux-ipc asserting no aibox_*/legends_core symbols (mirror pal-ci.yml's SDL symbol firewall at lines 165-172).

findings.title: Release pipeline never exercised: zero git tags, so tag-gated packaging, CPack NSIS/DMG, checksums, and the 80% coverage release gate have never run; version always falls back
findings.evidence: `git tag -l` returns nothing. packaging (ci.yml:771) and release-validation (ci.yml:846) are gated on refs/tags/v*. release-validation enforces src/app coverage >= 80% via lcov/bc that has never been evaluated. version.cmake matches 'v[0-9]*' tags that cannot match, so every build uses the '1.0.0+<hash>' fallback (version.cmake:46), and CPACK_PACKAGE_VERSION would carry a '+' into NSIS. RELEASING.md documents a release branch/tag workflow that has never been performed.
findings.recommendation: Perform a release dry-run now: push a v0.9.0-rc.1 tag from a throwaway branch, let packaging and release-validation run end-to-end, fix the fallout (coverage threshold, cpack/NSIS, version string). Add workflow_dispatch to release-validation so it can be rehearsed without tags.

findings.title: PRs targeting develop bypass the primary CI pipeline
findings.evidence: ci.yml restricts pull_request to branches [main, master], and pal-ci.yml likewise, but RELEASING.md's branch model routes feature/* PRs into develop. Such PRs get only sprint2-checks (Python lint + one test job) and module-dag (whose build jobs are schedule-gated at module-dag.yml:127,160). The main build+test matrix runs only post-merge on push to develop.
findings.recommendation: Add develop to pull_request.branches in ci.yml and pal-ci.yml (or remove the branch filter) so feature PRs are gated before merge.

findings.title: Dependency vulnerability scan is a no-op (osv-scanner fed a CMake file as a lockfile, errors swallowed) while roadmap marks REQ-SEC-028 'Done'
findings.evidence: ci.yml runs `./osv-scanner --lockfile cmake/dependencies.cmake || true` — osv-scanner does not support CMake files as lockfiles, so the command always fails and is swallowed by `|| true` plus `continue-on-error: true`; the binary is fetched from releases/latest unpinned; the job only runs on schedule/dispatch. roadmap.md:1470 lists 'dependency scanning (REQ-SEC-028)' as Fully implemented and roadmap.md:3279 marks it Done.
findings.recommendation: Generate an SBOM (CycloneDX/SPDX) from the pinned dependency versions plus the vendored DOSBox-X fork and scan that; pin the scanner version; remove `|| true`; downgrade REQ-SEC-028 status to partial until the scan produces real signal.

findings.title: No compiler caching and heavy workflow duplication: the 1M-line vendored engine is rebuilt cold up to ~12 times per push against 15-minute timeouts
findings.evidence: No workflow configures ccache/sccache; the only actions/cache entries cover build/_deps/sdl3-* sources. ci.yml linux (x2 compilers), linux-ipc, windows, coverage, sprint2-checks multi-instance, pal-ci's seven ungated jobs, and module-dag each compile the full engine from scratch. ci.yml linux has timeout-minutes: 15. CIFix.md itself states CI is duplicated across the four workflows causing one root cause to appear as several failures.
findings.recommendation: Add ccache keyed on compiler+flags; consolidate pal-ci's always-on jobs into the main matrix or path-gate them; reduce sprint2-checks to its Python lint role (its full-test job duplicates the linux job).

findings.title: Dependency pinning is mutable-tag-based, duplicated, and directly violated by pal-ci building SDL3 from upstream main; Actions not SHA-pinned
findings.evidence: All FetchContent pins are git tags (gsl-lite v1.0.0, SDL3 release-3.2.8, googletest v1.14.0, benchmark v1.8.3) with no SHA or URL_HASH; DEPENDENCIES.md:16 claims these make builds 'reproducible'. engine/CMakeLists.txt:330 hardcodes GIT_TAG v1.14.0 instead of using LEGENDS_DEP_GOOGLETEST_TAG (two declarations for the same dependency can drift). pal-ci.yml:98 does `git clone --depth 1 https://github.com/libsdl-org/SDL.git -b main` — unpinned upstream HEAD on every PAL push (recent 'Stabilize optional SDL backend CI' commits are consistent with chasing a moving SDL). Actions are tag-pinned (@v4/@v5) and osv-scanner comes from releases/latest.
findings.recommendation: Convert LEGENDS_DEP_*_TAG to commit SHAs (tag in comment/DEPENDENCIES.md); make engine consume the root pin variable; pin pal-ci's SDL3 build to release-3.2.8; SHA-pin third-party GitHub Actions.

findings.title: Committed UTF-16 build logs show the Windows clang dev preset failing to compile and link; that toolchain (and the presets' MinGW default) has zero CI coverage

findings.title: L5 residual: project_legends SDL2 target still unbuildable on Windows (hardcoded mingw32/SDL2main link, nonexistent external/SDL2 tree); src/main.cpp now exists and Linux SDL2 builds in CI
findings.evidence: src/main.cpp exists at HEAD (it did not at the 2026-02-24 audit) and pal-ci's sdl2-tests job builds the SDL2 path on Linux via find_package(SDL2 REQUIRED). findings.title: Hardening flags are configuration-blind: _FORTIFY_SOURCE=2 injected into -O0 Debug builds where it is inert and risks glibc #warning escalation under Tier A -Werror
findings.evidence: legends_compile_options applies `-fstack-protector-strong -D_FORTIFY_SOURCE=2` unconditionally alongside `$<$<CONFIG:Debug>:-g -O0>`; Tier A targets add -Werror. _FORTIFY_SOURCE does nothing at -O0, glibc's features.h emits `#warning _FORTIFY_SOURCE requires compiling with optimization` in that case (Debug Linux jobs: linux-ipc, all sanitizer presets), and explicit =2 can collide with Ubuntu's default =3. The committed build_log.txt shows the flag also being passed on Windows where the CRT ignores it.
findings.recommendation: Gate the define: `$<$<NOT:$<CONFIG:Debug>>:-D_FORTIFY_SOURCE=2>` and restrict to glibc/GNU-CRT platforms.

findings.title: Warning policy weaker than documented: test targets opt out of -Werror despite 'tests should be strict too', header-guard CI check cannot fail, clang-tidy warnings unbounded
findings.evidence: Comment at CMakeLists.txt:776 says 'Tier A - tests should be strict too' but legends_unit_tests gets -Wno-error on GCC/Clang (:811-813) and legends_integration_tests likewise (:1006-1008); committed build_output.txt shows engine tests emitting ignored-[[nodiscard]] warnings. The abi-check header-guard step only echoes WARNING lines and always exits 0. The clang-tidy job fails only on 'error:' lines, so modernize/bugprone/performance findings accumulate untracked.
findings.recommendation: Burn down test-target nodiscard warnings and remove -Wno-error; make the header-guard check exit non-zero; record a clang-tidy warning-count baseline that may only decrease.

verdict.note: Verified all cited evidence directly. (1) cmake/VerifyGPLIsolation.cmake:8 documents 'include(VerifyGPLIsolation)' usage but repo-wide grep finds no include() call in any CMake file — only the module itself, audit docs, and an openspec spec example. (2) ModuleDAG.cmake:124 hardcodes MODULES to legends_core/legends_pal/aibox_core and legends_verify_all_dags (191-213) verifies only those 3 targets, while ModuleManifest.cmake:63-68 defines LEGENDS_DAG_ entries for legends_ipc/legends_proxy/legends_engine_host that nothing checks (legends_verify_dag never called on them anywhere). (3) The GPL constraints at CMakeLists.txt:361-362 and 422-423 are comments only. (4) tasks.md:54 confirms unchecked '8.3 Linker verification: verify_gpl_isolation.py + CMake integration'. (5) No mitigation elsewhere: the linux-ipc CI job (ci.yml:95-127) builds with LEGENDS_USE_IPC=ON but no PAL backend and has no nm/symbol step; project_legends is guarded by if(PAL_BACKEND_SDL2) at CMakeLists.txt:1151, so even if VerifyGPLIsolation were included it would be a no-op in that job; tests/scripts/test_verify_gpl_isolation.py only tests the script on synthetic map files and is not registered in ctest or any workflow. (6) pal-ci.yml:165-172 SDL symbol firewall exists exactly as cited as the pattern to mirror. Severity high is justified: a stray target_link_libraries(legends_proxy legends_core) would pass configure and all CI silently, defeating the project's central GPL-isolation promise. Finding could not be refuted on any point.

Verified, finding holds. (1) Zero tags confirmed three ways: `git tag -l` empty, `git ls-remote --tags origin` empty, `gh api repos/CharlesHoskinson/ProjectLegends/tags` and `gh release list` both empty. (2) All cited lines say what is claimed: ci.yml:771 and ci.yml:846 gate packaging and release-validation on startsWith(github.ref, 'refs/tags/v'); ci.yml:874-888 enforce src/app lcov coverage >= 80% via bc only in that tag-gated job; version.cmake:24 matches 'v[0-9]*' tags. (3) Fallback verified live: `git describe --tags --always --dirty --match "v[0-9]*"` outputs `ef11f20-dirty` (bare hash), failing the semver regex at version.cmake:37, so line 46 yields `1.0.0+ef11f20-dirty` (PROJECT_VERSION=1.0.0 at CMakeLists.txt:14); packaging.cmake:14 feeds that '+'-bearing string into CPACK_PACKAGE_VERSION with NSIS selected on WIN32 (lines 17-18). (4) Mitigation search found none: the only other coverage job (ci.yml:674-730) is explicitly report-only ("no minimum threshold is enforced by CI yet", line 716); no other workflow (module-dag.yml, pal-ci.yml, sprint2-checks.yml) or script runs cpack/generate_checksums; no release/* branch has ever existed. The ci.yml `on:` block does include tags: ["v[0-9]*"], so the wiring is plausible but unproven — exactly the finding's point. Minor caveat: the implication that '+' breaks NSIS is plausible but untested speculation; the literal claim (CPACK_PACKAGE_VERSION carries '+') is accurate. High severity is justified given the repo's release-readiness plan and feature/beta-blockers branch indicate an upcoming release relying on this never-run path.

findings.title: Merge gate stripped: sanitizers, fuzzing, TLA+, static analysis demoted to nightly/manual-only on 2026-06-08
findings.evidence: git show 6900e7a ('Stabilize CI and RuntimeHost adoption', 2026-06-08) changed sanitizers from 'main || master || schedule' to schedule/workflow_dispatch only, fuzz from 'schedule || pull_request || main' to schedule/dispatch only, and made tlaplus/static-analysis/macOS conditional; jobs renamed 'Optional ...'. The fuzz job's 'PR: Quick fuzz' step (ci.yml:503) is dead code since the job-level if excludes pull_request. TSan/MSan were already allow_failure:true (ci.yml:351-365).
