findings.title: Determinism and save/load roundtrip tests assert on Fast-mode hash that excludes guest RAM, CPU GPRs/EIP, and VRAM
findings.evidence: All hash-based tests call legends_get_state_hash -> dosbox_lib_get_state_hash which hard-codes HashMode::Fast (dosbox_library.cpp:684). Fast mode hashes cycle counters only for CPU (no GPRs/EIP, dosbox_context.cpp:103-118) and page config for memory; guest RAM is hashed only in HashMode::Full (state_hash.cpp:301-303) which nothing calls; VRAM absent even from Full. H7 is partially fixed (Full now hashes RAM, not just a 'FULL_MODE' string) but the gap moved into the test oracle: TwoRunsProduceSameHash, MidpointSaveLoadMatchesStraightRun, RepeatedSaveLoadCycle, and legends_verify_determinism cannot detect divergence or corruption in the bulk of machine state.
findings.recommendation: Expose Full-mode hashing to tests (legends_get_state_hash_ex or test hook), extend Full to VRAM/GPRs with Phase B, switch determinism/roundtrip tests to it, and add a direct write-pattern/save/perturb/load/read-pattern memory test that bypasses hashing.

findings.title: 8 of 33 registered integration test files are one-line GTEST_SKIP 'Not yet implemented' stubs, including replay determinism and save-state compat
findings.evidence: Each file is exactly two lines, e.g. TEST(ReplayDeterminismStub, NotYetImplemented) { GTEST_SKIP() << "Not yet implemented"; }. Stubs: replay_determinism, save_state_compat, visual_regression, golden_visual, determinism_hash, cross_platform_smoke, frame_timing, pairwise_config — all registered in CMakeLists.txt:941-979 and reporting green/skipped every CI run. These are exactly the headline product promises (deterministic replay, save-state compatibility, visual regression).
findings.recommendation: Implement replay-determinism (record trace, replay from save, compare Full-mode hashes) and save-state-compat (golden V3/V4 fixture blobs) first; convert remaining stubs to tracked issues and delete the stub files so skips stop masquerading as suite breadth.

findings.title: IPC/process-isolation path has no enabled E2E or parity coverage; dispatcher tested for 8 of 43 message cases, proxy only for not-connected errors
findings.evidence: Only true cross-process test is TEST_F(IpcIntegrationTest, DISABLED_FullE2E) (never runs; also GTEST_SKIPs at lines 66/79). engine_dispatcher.cpp has 43 case MsgType:: handlers; test_engine_dispatcher.cpp covers 8, all happy-path with no malformed/truncated payload cases. test_proxy_api.cpp asserts only NOT_INITIALIZED/NOT_SUPPORTED when unconnected. In the linux-ipc CI job, legends_unit_tests still links legends_app->legends_core (only project_legends links legends_proxy, CMakeLists.txt:1173-1180), so the proxy->pipe->engine_host chain is never exercised under assertion. Commit 274ef4d 'Add RuntimeHost proxy parity' added openspec docs and dispatcher cases, zero parity tests; src/app/runtime_host.cpp (655 lines) has no direct unit test.
findings.recommendation: Un-disable FullE2E with engine-host path discovery and run it in linux-ipc; add a parameterized in-process vs proxy parity suite diffing step results, text captures, and hashes; add table-driven malformed-payload dispatch tests over all 43 cases.

findings.title: Fuzzing is shallow: CRC32 wall blocks the load-state fuzzers past the header, no IPC fuzz target, 30-60s nightly-only budget, no persisted corpus
findings.evidence: legends_load_state verifies CRC32 before any section parsing (legends_embed_api.cpp:2072-2073, V2 path at 2335); the custom mutator patches magic/version bytes but never the checksum, so mutated inputs die at the CRC check and deep deserialization (including the H9 reinterpret_cast paths) is effectively unfuzzed. grep -i ipc tests/fuzz/ -> no matches: the message codec/dispatcher trust boundary (108 msg types, 64MB cap) has no fuzz target. fuzz_input_injection covers only key/mouse/step, not text_input (known M2 bug) or key_event_ext. Corpus regenerated from scratch each run (ci.yml:499-500); whole job nightly/dispatch-only since 6900e7a.
findings.recommendation: Recompute CRC after mutation in the custom mutator (or LEGENDS_FUZZING define downgrading CRC mismatch); persist corpus via actions/cache; add fuzz_ipc_codec and fuzz_engine_dispatch targets; fuzz legends_text_input.

findings.title: L8 sentinel invalid-handle destroy pattern fixed; test now proves rejection and instance survival (H5 also closed)
findings.evidence: test_legends_embed_lifecycle.cpp:210-212 passes fake handle 0xDEADBEEF to legends_destroy and asserts EXPECT_NE(err, LEGENDS_OK), then verifies the real instance is still alive and destroys it cleanly. get_instance() (legends_embed_api.cpp:79-82) now returns the instance only when handle == active instance — no g_active_instance fallback remains.
findings.recommendation: Mark L8 and H5 resolved in AUDIT.md; see test-weak-07 for assertion-free residue in older tests that should now pin exact error codes.

findings.title: Assertion-free 'no crash' tests persist after the H5 fix made exact error-code assertions possible
findings.evidence: InvalidFakeHandle discards the error with (void)err and comments 'might be NULL_HANDLE, INVALID_STATE, or even OK'; DoubleDestroyIsSafe: 'err2 can be OK or an error'; OperationsOnDestroyedHandleDontCrash ignores every return; InvalidHandlesRejected asserts nothing despite its name ('or accept if handle validation is minimal'). Since get_instance is now strict, all have deterministic correct answers (LEGENDS_ERR_NULL_HANDLE); a regression reintroducing the H5 fallback would not be caught by the tests named for it.
findings.recommendation: Assert exact error codes in all four tests; grep the suite for '(void)err' and triage remaining assertion-free calls.

findings.title: API coverage map: legends_set_ttf_font has zero tests; 15 device APIs have null-handle-only coverage; capability-gated APIs never asserted in headless-only CI
findings.evidence: Per-API grep of all 50 legends_* functions: legends_set_ttf_font appears in zero test files. pc98 (x2), glide (x2), printer (x3), ipx (x4), midi (x3), capture_midi_audio are referenced substantively only by test_phase3_bridge.cpp, which asserts LEGENDS_ERR_NULL_HANDLE against nullptr — no live-handle test exists. Video capture (start/stop/is_capturing), mount happy paths, and drive event callbacks skip in headless ('not available in headless mode', 'backend not wired in headless build'), and every CI job configures -DLEGENDS_HEADLESS=ON, so they never execute under assertion in CI.
findings.recommendation: Add a live-handle contract test per device API pinning the defined headless return code (e.g. NOT_SUPPORTED); add a TTF font test with a fixture; run one SDL2 dummy-driver job in ci.yml so capability-gated paths execute.

findings.title: SDL backend tests are path-filtered/nightly only, and 'Relax SDL backend startup event tests' deleted an assertion instead of refining it
findings.evidence: Commit 911692f replaced EXPECT_EQ(count, 0u) after input init with (void)input->poll(events, 10) in both SDL2 and SDL3 tests — the test now verifies only that poll doesn't crash. The stated reason (backends may emit window/device events at startup) justifies a type-whitelist assertion, not none. pal-ci.yml triggers only on src/pal/include/cmake/test_pal path changes plus nightly cron, so changes in src/legends or src/app never run any SDL test pre-merge. By contrast, sibling commit 8fdd4c6 (dummy drivers + GTEST_SKIP on missing audio device) is a defensible stabilization.
findings.recommendation: Restore the startup-event test as a whitelist assertion (each returned event must be Window/Device type); broaden pal-ci path filters to src/legends/** and src/app/** or move the SDL2-dummy job into ci.yml.

findings.title: Soak/endurance suite can never run: no workflow sets LEGENDS_SOAK_ENABLED and the soak-label cmake module does not exist
findings.evidence: test_soak_endurance.cpp skips unless LEGENDS_SOAK_ENABLED/LEGENDS_SOAK_SHORT is set; no workflow sets either (grep of .github/workflows finds only comments and a --label-exclude). CMakeLists.txt:1021 references cmake/SoakTestLabels.cmake '(if present)' — the file does not exist, so the soak label is never applied and the test-soak target acts on nothing. ci.yml header advertises 'nightly (cron): soak tests, fuzz' but the nightly schedule contains no soak step.
findings.recommendation: Add a nightly step running LEGENDS_SOAK_SHORT=1 ctest -R SoakEndurance; either write SoakTestLabels.cmake or remove the dead label plumbing and stale comments.

findings.title: Benchmarks (emulation, PAL, IPC overhead) are never built or run in any CI workflow; no performance regression tracking
findings.evidence: LEGENDS_BUILD_BENCHMARKS defaults OFF (CMakeLists.txt:1078); grep -rn bench .github/workflows/ returns zero matches; no baseline JSON or comparison script exists. The three google-benchmark targets (564 lines total) bit-rot silently since no configuration compiles them, and IPC-mode per-call overhead — the exact thing bench_ipc_overhead measures — can regress without detection.
findings.recommendation: Add a nightly job building with -DLEGENDS_BUILD_BENCHMARKS=ON (catches bit-rot at minimum), emit --benchmark_format=json, and compare against a checked-in baseline with a generous regression threshold.

findings.title: Dead/orphaned test assets: 3 uncompilable integration tests calling nonexistent legends_init(), 6 unregistered engine tests, 3 unused COM fixtures
findings.evidence: test_context_synchronization.cpp and test_error_propagation.cpp call legends_init(handle), which exists nowhere in include/ — they cannot compile and are absent from CMakeLists registration (as is test_dual_ffi.cpp). engine/tests/unit has 6 files not in engine/tests/CMakeLists.txt:23-92, including test_serialization_completeness.cpp (executable assertions documenting the H1 keyboard truncation, never built) and test_multi_instance_smoke.cpp. tests/fixtures/{counter,graphics,input}.com are referenced only by the fixtures README — the prior audit's 'no test runs a real DOS program' gap remains open.
findings.recommendation: Delete or modernize the three uncompilable stubs; register salvageable engine tests (at minimum test_serialization_completeness.cpp); write the COM-fixture execution test (mount, run counter.com, assert text output).

findings.title: Coverage is report-only; the single enforced 80% threshold covers only src/app/ and runs only on release tags
findings.evidence: Coverage job writes 'Coverage policy: report-only; no minimum threshold is enforced by CI yet.' (ci.yml:716). The only enforced gate is in release-validation (tag pushes only) and extracts only '*/src/app/*' before checking >= 80% (ci.yml:879-888) — src/legends, src/legends_ipc, src/legends_proxy, src/engine_host, src/pal are outside every enforced gate. lcov error suppression widened in 46e6bd5 to mismatch,gcov,negative and unused,empty. Exclusions themselves are honest (/usr, _deps, tests only; engine and src remain in the report).
findings.recommendation: Take a baseline and enforce a no-decrease ratchet on src/legends + src/legends_ipc + src/legends_proxy line coverage in the per-push coverage job; document each --ignore-errors flag.

findings.title: README 'tests: 1500+ passing' is a static hardcoded badge; 'passing' includes 65+ skips, 8 stub files, and a DISABLED E2E
findings.evidence: README.md:8 is a static shields.io badge linking to nothing, not CI-generated. Actual TEST macro counts: ~2,788 under tests/ and ~1,878 under engine/tests (registered subset), so the figure is stale-low rather than inflated — but the green 'passing' framing silently includes 65+ GTEST_SKIP sites, the 8 'Not yet implemented' stubs, the never-run soak suite, and the DISABLED_ IPC E2E. Build/coverage badges on adjacent lines are equally static.
findings.recommendation: Replace with CI-generated workflow and Codecov badges (a Codecov upload already exists at ci.yml:726-731), or state the count with a date and skip tally.

report.summary: The suite is broad and much of it is real — ~2,788 TEST macros in tests/ plus ~1,878 in engine/tests, a genuine boot-to-DOS-prompt test, exact-assertion save-state security tests, and prior finding L8 (and underlying H5) properly fixed. But three structural problems undercut it: (1) commit 6900e7a (2026-06-08, one day before this audit) demoted all four sanitizers, fuzzing, TLA+ checking, static analysis, and macOS jobs to nightly/manual-only, so the merge gate is now just Linux+Windows headless build-and-test — flakiness was suppressed by demotion, not fixed; (2) every determinism and save/load roundtrip test asserts on the Fast-mode state hash, which excludes guest RAM, CPU GPRs/EIP, and VRAM, so the headline invariants are asserted-by-sentinel; (3) the IPC/GPL-isolation path has no enabled end-to-end test (the only cross-process test is DISABLED_), the dispatcher is tested for 8 of 43 cases, and no in-process-vs-proxy parity suite exists despite a 'proxy parity' commit that added only docs. Eight of 33 integration test files — including replay determinism and save-state compat — are one-line skip stubs; fuzzers are walled off by an unfixed CRC check; benchmarks and the soak suite never run anywhere.
sprint_recommendations: Restore the merge gate: ASan/UBSan plus a 30s fuzz smoke back on merge-to-main, fix the dead PR-fuzz step, nightly soak step with LEGENDS_SOAK_SHORT=1, and a coverage ratchet on src/legends*/src/legends_ipc/src/legends_proxy (test-ci-01, test-cov-13, test-soak-10)

Strengthen the oracles: plumb Full-mode (RAM-inclusive) state hashing into the determinism and roundtrip tests, add a direct write-pattern/save/load/read-back memory test, and implement the replay-determinism and save-state-compat integration tests that are currently skip stubs (test-oracle-02, test-stub-03)

Test the trust boundary: enable the IPC FullE2E in the linux-ipc job, build an in-process-vs-proxy parity suite over the 43 dispatch cases with malformed-payload table tests, add fuzz_ipc_codec/fuzz_engine_dispatch targets, and fix the CRC wall in the load-state fuzz mutator with a persisted corpus (test-ipc-04, test-fuzz-05)

Burn down dishonest residue: exact error-code assertions in the no-crash tests, live-handle contract tests for the 15 device APIs and legends_set_ttf_font, delete/register orphaned test files, wire the COM fixtures into a real DOS-program execution test, and replace the static '1500+ passing' badge with CI-generated badges (test-weak-07, test-api-08, test-dead-12, test-readme-14)

verdict.note: Verified, could not refute. (1) All cited lines match: C:\projectLegends\.github\workflows\ci.yml:333 (sanitizers), :431 (static-analysis), :474 (fuzz), :554 (tlaplus) are gated `schedule || workflow_dispatch` only, jobs renamed 'Optional ...'; TSan/MSan allow_failure at :355/:365 as the finding states. (2) `git show 6900e7a` (2026-06-08, 'Stabilize CI and RuntimeHost adoption') shows the exact claimed before/after: sanitizers were `main || master || schedule`, fuzz was `schedule || pull_request || main || master`; static-analysis/tlaplus/macOS/SDL3 lanes and dependency-scan (REQ-SEC-028, not even cited by the finding) gained schedule/dispatch-only conditions. Follow-up commit 46e6bd5 same day restored nothing. (3) Dead-code claim confirmed: step at ci.yml:503-504 has `if: github.event_name == 'pull_request'` but the job-level if excludes pull_request, so it can never run. (4) Header comment ci.yml:10 still claims 'merge-to-main: + sanitizers' — stale as claimed. PR/merge path inventory matches (linux, linux-ipc, windows, abi-check, report-only coverage). Mitigations examined and insufficient to refute: nightly 03:00 UTC cron still runs the demoted jobs (post-merge detection only, failures block nothing); pal-ci.yml runs ASan on PAL-path PRs but only with --gtest_filter=ContractGate_Lifecycle*; the demotion was deliberate and documented in CIFix.md ('non-blocking until green') and openspec change ci-stabilization-and-coverage-control, but no task tracks re-promotion and all spec tasks are checked complete. High severity is justified: ASan/UBSan were passing hard gates on merge-to-main and memory-safety regressions can now land gated only by build+unit tests, with the workflow header masking the change.

Verified: all 8 claimed stub files (replay_determinism, save_state_compat, visual_regression, golden_visual, determinism_hash, cross_platform_smoke, frame_timing, pairwise_config) are exactly two lines each, containing only GTEST_SKIP() << "Not yet implemented" (confirmed by reading the 4 cited files and grepping tests/integration; sizes 111-118 bytes). All 8 are registered in legends_integration_tests at CMakeLists.txt:964-973 with gtest_discover_tests, and ci.yml runs ctest broadly, so they appear as skipped/green in CI. Attempted refutation via mitigation search: test_workflow_determinism.cpp and test_workflow_saveload.cpp (incl. DeterministicReplayAfterLoad) provide real same-version determinism/round-trip coverage, but they run on the Headless backend (the file's own comment at lines 64-66 says full emulation isn't running), test_v2_load_safety.cpp only tests rejection of malformed V2 blobs (not V3/V4 cross-version compat), and visual regression has zero real coverage despite CMakeLists.txt:984-987 compiling ssim.cpp specifically for the (stub) visual tests. README.md headlines deterministic execution and save/state replay, supporting the framing. One minor inaccuracy: the count is 8 of 31 registered integration files (34 on disk, 3 unregistered), not 8 of 33 — immaterial. High severity is justified for save-state compat and visual regression; determinism is partially mitigated by the headless workflow tests.

Verified every cited claim against source. (1) test_ipc_integration.cpp:42 is TEST_F(IpcIntegrationTest, DISABLED_FullE2E) with GTEST_SKIP at lines 66/79; it is the only cross-process test and nothing in scripts/CI passes --gtest_also_run_disabled_tests, so it never runs. (2) engine_dispatcher.cpp has exactly 43 'case MsgType::' handlers; test_engine_dispatcher.cpp has exactly 8 TEST_Fs (7 distinct cases + unknown-type default) — '8 of 43' accurate; minor nit that DispatchUnknownReturnsError is a negative test. (3) Proxy claim is UNDERSTATED: test_proxy_api.cpp is wrapped in #ifdef LEGENDS_USE_IPC, but legends_unit_tests never gets that define (CMakeLists.txt:800-806) and never links legends_proxy (only legends_proxy propagates LEGENDS_USE_IPC PUBLIC, line 429-433) — so even the not-connected tests are dead code in every build; test_proxy_connection.cpp only simulates the proxy with raw ControlChannel calls, never executing proxy_api.cpp/proxy_connection.cpp. (4) CMakeLists.txt:1173-1180 confirmed: only project_legends links legends_proxy; legends_unit_tests links legends_app which PUBLIC-links legends_core (line 571-577), so the linux-ipc CI job (ci.yml:95-127, -DLEGENDS_USE_IPC=ON) only test-f's that binaries exist and runs ctest against the monolithic engine — proxy->pipe->engine_host chain never asserted. (5) git show 274ef4d confirmed 'Add RuntimeHost proxy parity': +418 proxy_api lines, +323 dispatcher lines, 3 openspec dirs; tests added were 3 happy-path dispatcher tests and 2 capability tests, zero proxy-vs-in-process parity tests. (6) runtime_host.cpp is exactly 655 lines; only RuntimeHost mention in tests/ is test_ai_screen_context.cpp (not a direct test). Partial mitigation found: per-message TooSmall deserialize tests exist in test_ipc_messages.cpp and dispatcher propagates deserialize errors, so the malformed-payload recommendation has lower marginal value — but the E2E/parity gap stands. High severity justified: IPC mode is the GPL-isolation shipping configuration with a dedicated CI job that passes while exercising none of the IPC runtime path.

All four evidence legs verified against source. (1) CRC wall: legends_embed_api.cpp checks CRC32 before section parsing at 2335-2338 (V3) and 2072-2075 (V2); the custom mutator in fuzz_legends_load_state.cpp:56-90 fixes magic/version but never the checksum, and grep finds no FUZZING define in src/ that bypasses CRC — body mutations cannot pass (2^-32), so only the 96-byte header is meaningfully fuzzed. (2) No IPC fuzz target: tests/fuzz/ has only 4 targets, zero 'ipc' matches; the layer exists with exactly 108 MsgType entries (message_types.h) and kMaxPayloadSize = 64MB (message_codec.h:22). (3) fuzz_input_injection.cpp:20-47 dispatches only key_event/mouse_event/step_cycles; legends_text_input and key_event_ext are uncovered. (4) ci.yml:474 gates the fuzz job to schedule/workflow_dispatch (commit 6900e7a removed PR/main triggers, leaving the 30s PR step dead code), and the corpus is regenerated each run with no actions/cache entry for it. Mitigations checked: test_legends_embed_security.cpp deterministically covers header-offset validation (header is outside the CRC region), and the load path uses defensive VALIDATE_* macros and memcpy-to-aligned-locals — but that post-CRC body-parsing code is exactly what fuzzing cannot reach. Minor stale detail: the evidence cites 'H9 reinterpret_cast paths' but the load path now uses memcpy (H9 appears fixed). Severity: high is defensible since save-state load and the IPC codec/dispatcher are untrusted-input trust boundaries with effectively vacuous or zero fuzz coverage, though it is a coverage gap rather than a demonstrated vulnerability — medium-high would also be reasonable.

report.summary: Recently refreshed docs are accurate — the README architecture diagram's counts (50 C APIs, 108 IPC message types, 89 structs, 43 dispatcher cases) all verified exactly against source, and RELEASING.md matches the real ci.yml job set. Everything older has drifted, in both directions: REQUIREMENTS.md still reports February GAP statuses for at least six requirements fixed in code since, TODO.md marks the same requirement IDs both complete and missing, and ARCHITECTURE.md documents a save-state format (96-byte header, LEGS magic, v2) contradicting both README (64 bytes) and code (DBXS, v3). Licensing is the most serious area: the repo root LICENSE is a bare MIT grant over a codebase that vendors a 1M-line GPL DOSBox-X fork (README falsely calls it a "multi-component license overview"), docs say GPL-2.0-only while every actual SPDX tag says GPL-2.0-or-later, the MIT proxy and "proprietary shell" compile against a GPL-licensed legends_embed.h that the isolation design never addresses, and the linker-map GPL verification the docs claim CI runs is never included in any build. Finally, the README capability bullet "Wasm sandbox support" references wasm.md and wit/legends-emulator.wit files that have never existed in git history while TODO.md says Wasm is 0/50 not started.

findings.title: Root LICENSE file is a bare MIT grant over a GPL codebase, mislabeled as a multi-component overview
findings.evidence: LICENSE contains verbatim MIT text covering 'the Software' with no component scoping; README.md:312/367 describe it as 'Multi-component license overview'; COPYING is full GPLv2; engine/ vendors GPL DOSBox-X (engine/src/cpu/cpu.cpp:4-7 'version 2 ... or any later version'). Introduced by commit 8e78bfe as a 21-line file (the MIT text).
findings.recommendation: Replace LICENSE content with an actual component->license->directory overview pointing at COPYING and the MIT-scoped dirs; fix the README/CHANGELOG descriptions so SPDX scanners and GitHub detection stop reading the project as MIT.

findings.title: GPL-2.0-only vs GPL-2.0-or-later: README/CONTRIBUTING say -only, all 100+ actual SPDX tags and DEPENDENCIES.md say -or-later
findings.evidence: SPDX tally: 107 src/ files + 9 include/ files tagged GPL-2.0-or-later, zero tagged GPL-2.0-only, while CONTRIBUTING.md mandates GPL-2.0-only headers and README declares 'SPDX expression: GPL-2.0-only AND MIT'. README's claim that -only is 'consistent with DOSBox-X' is wrong: vendored upstream files are GPL-2.0-or-later. legends_embed.h has no SPDX tag at all; engine/ ships no license text of its own.
findings.recommendation: Pick one GPL version expression (simplest: GPL-2.0-or-later matching the file tags and upstream), align README/CONTRIBUTING/NOTICE/DEPENDENCIES.md, add an SPDX tag to legends_embed.h, and add a CI lint comparing SPDX tags to the per-directory policy.

findings.title: Non-GPL shell story glosses over the GPL-licensed API header; design doc calls the GPL-tagged shell 'proprietary'
findings.evidence: MIT-tagged proxy_api.cpp #includes GPL-licensed legends_embed.h (header says 'Licensed under GNU GPL v2.0'; CONTRIBUTING assigns include/legends/ GPL-2.0-only) while DEPENDENCIES.md:18 claims the MIT proxy 'does not link any GPL code'. Design doc says the shell is a 'proprietary application shell' with 'zero GPL object code' but CONTRIBUTING.md:258 assigns src/app GPL-2.0-only and src/app/application.cpp:1 is tagged GPL-2.0-or-later. README Quick Start statically links the GPL core and advertises Rust/Python FFI with no statement of the GPL obligations on in-process embedders (only ARCHITECTURE.md:553 mentions it).
findings.recommendation: Dual-license or MIT-license legends_embed.h explicitly and document it in TDD-LIC-001; reconcile the proprietary-shell claim with src/app's GPL tags; add an explicit 'GPL obligations when embedding in-process' paragraph to README's License section.

findings.title: 'Wasm sandbox support' advertised as a capability; referenced wasm.md and wit/legends-emulator.wit have never existed in git history

verdict.note: Verified all citations directly. LICENSE:1-21 is verbatim bare MIT over "the Software" with no scoping (confirmed by Read). README.md:312 and :367 both call it "Multi-component license overview" (confirmed); CHANGELOG.md:50-51 says the same (cited as :52, trivially off). COPYING is full GPLv2. engine/src/cpu/cpu.cpp:1-17 carries the DOSBox GPL-2.0-or-later header, and other engine/src files have GPL SPDX headers. git show 8e78bfe confirms LICENSE was added as a 21-line file, and the commit message itself says "LICENSE (MIT)" — contradicting the docs. Refutation attempts failed: per-file SPDX MIT headers in include/legends_ipc/ and the accurate README License section (351-364) inform careful readers, but nothing overrides the root LICENSE that GitHub/SPDX scanners read; there is no engine/COPYING or per-directory scoping (only vendored libchdr lzma/zstd LICENSE files), and NOTICE only covers third-party attribution. Severity critical is justified: the root LICENSE legally purports to grant MIT rights (sublicense/sell) over vendored GPLv2 code the copyright holder cannot relicense, creating GPL-violation exposure for downstream users. Recommendation in the finding is correct.

Confirmed all cited evidence. README.md:355/364 declare GPL-2.0-only ('consistent with DOSBox-X') and 'GPL-2.0-only AND MIT'; CONTRIBUTING.md:226-233 mandates GPL-2.0-only headers; DEPENDENCIES.md:18 says 'GPL-2.0-or-later license'. Independent repo-wide tally (excluding audit-wiki/build): 200 files tagged GPL-2.0-or-later, 48 MIT, 2 Zlib, ZERO GPL-2.0-only — the only -only strings are in CONTRIBUTING.md and the audit report itself, so the finding's 116-file count was conservative. engine/src/cpu/cpu.cpp:4-7 carries DOSBox 'version 2 or (at your option) any later version' boilerplate, refuting README's claim that -only is consistent with upstream. include/legends/legends_embed.h has no SPDX tag (only ambiguous 'GPL v2.0' prose); engine/ contains only 1-byte stubs, no license text. No mitigation exists: no SPDX lint in any .github/workflows file; scripts/verify_gpl_isolation.py checks linker-map symbols, not headers. Bonus contradiction: root LICENSE (README calls it 'multi-component overview') is pure MIT text. High severity is justified for a compliance finding: docs vs file headers grant materially different rights, and contributors following CONTRIBUTING would mix -only into an -or-later tree, in a project whose architecture centers on GPL isolation.

Verified all six citations; every quote is accurate. proxy_api.cpp is SPDX MIT (line 1) and includes legends_embed.h (line 6), whose own header text (line 7) says GPL v2.0 and which CONTRIBUTING.md:253 assigns GPL-2.0-only — yet DEPENDENCIES.md:18 claims the MIT proxy 'does not link any GPL code' with no mention of the GPL header at the ABI boundary (true at object-link level per CMakeLists.txt:422-427, but the compile-time dependency is undocumented and the design doc TDD-LIC-001 never addresses header licensing). Design doc line 5 verbatim calls the shell a 'proprietary application shell' with 'zero GPL object code', contradicted by CONTRIBUTING.md:258 (src/app GPL-2.0-only) and src/app/application.cpp:1 (GPL-2.0-or-later — also inconsistent with '-only'). README Quick Start (154-185) embeds in-process against legends_core (STATIC lib, CMakeLists.txt:186) and README:29 advertises Rust/Python FFI, while the README License section (351-368) omits in-process embedder obligations; ARCHITECTURE.md:553 is the only mention. Refutation attempts failed: NOTICE is third-party-only, root LICENSE is plain MIT text (an extra inconsistency vs the GPL-2.0 README badge), no doc reconciles the contradictions. Only caveat: whether #include of an API header legally creates a derivative is contested, but the internal documentation contradictions are real regardless. High severity is justified because GPL isolation is the project's core advertised feature and the contradictions could mislead downstream embedders into license violations.

Verified every citation. README.md:28 advertises 'Wasm sandbox support' present-tense under Capabilities; ARCHITECTURE.md:611-716 claims 'The project supports an optional Wasm/WASI build target' and 'CI enforces parity (REQ-WASM-026, REQ-WASM-040)'; CMakeLists.txt:452 references wasm.md/wit/ and line 478 lists SOURCES wit/legends-emulator.wit. Confirmed wasm.md and wit/ are absent from the working tree and `git log --all -- wasm.md` / `-- wit` are empty (never committed). Word-precise grep of .github/workflows for wasm|wasi|wasmtime returns zero matches, so the CI-parity claim is false. Grep for LEGENDS_BUILD_WASM shows only the OFF-by-default CMake option and docs — no wasm code exists. Refutation attempts found only partial mitigations: README.md:309 marks wasm.md '(planned)' in the directory tree, TODO.md:20/258 honestly says NOT STARTED 0/50 documentation-only, and the dangling CMake target is gated behind LEGENDS_BUILD_WASM=ON plus wit-bindgen being installed (default builds unaffected). These do not cure the README Capabilities bullet or the present-tense ARCHITECTURE.md section. Severity: high is defensible because the false claim concerns a security boundary (sandboxed execution, default-deny capabilities) plus nonexistent CI enforcement that an embedder could rely on; downgrade to medium only if treated purely as a docs-accuracy issue since no default build or runtime behavior is affected. Recommendation in the finding is appropriate.
